# Foundation 05B: The Remaining Screens Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking. This plan is built for parallel execution: after the two groundwork tasks (G1, G2), seven tracks (S, B, D, N, A, C, P) run at the same time, each in its own git worktree, and the two Integration tasks run last. Plan 5C (the release, `2026-10-16-foundation-05c-release.md`) runs apart and merges before, after or beside it.

**Goal:** Every screen the Foundation still lacks (spec 11), over plans 3 and 4's api: the platform console at `/console` (sign-in with two-factor required of platform staff, the dashboard, onboarding, an organization's page with its members, support's impersonation and its subscription, plans and the policy, failed jobs and schedules, the platform log, platform staff, data protection), and the agency's remaining screens (the subscription's banners and locked screens with read-only shown on every change, the business profile and setup checklist, business files uploaded straight to storage with sensitive files, branding with the logo on documents, a sample quotation with its PDF and share links, the notification bell, choices and web push, the audit log viewer), each proven by unit tests and Playwright journeys against the real api, worker and console process.

**Architecture:**
- **The console is a section of the web app, `/console`** (ADR 0025): its routes in `apps/web/src/app/console/**`, its code in `apps/web/src/console/**`, which nothing else imports. Same origin is what lets support's impersonation work (Better Auth swaps the session cookie at `/api/auth`) and what spec 3 asks. It has its own TanStack query cache, in memory only, and its own tRPC client at `/api/platform/trpc`, typed by `type PlatformRouter` alone; the web app rewrites `/api/platform/*` to `CONSOLE_ORIGIN` before `/api/*`, and the service worker keeps no console page.
- **One sign-in page.** Platform staff sign in by email where everyone does and land on `/console`; the step screens bring them back with `?next=`. `staffProcedure` refuses `SET_UP_TWO_FACTOR` to staff without two-factor, the impersonation side door does too, and the code step never trusts the device on the way to the console.
- **The agency's new api** is one router per area (`attachments`, `documents`, `shareLinks`, `notifications`, `audit`, `organization.logo`), each registered by groundwork and filled by its track; the api context gains `db`, `files` and the VAPID public key (served by `notifications.push.publicKey`, so one build serves every environment).
- **What the subscription allows is shown as check 2 decides it** (ADR 0026): `useWriteAccess(kind)` mirrors `assertLifecycleAllows` from `subscription.get`, so a refused change is disabled with the reason, and taking access away stays open.
- **Files go from the browser straight to storage** (`uploadFile`, presigned PUT with the signed headers), allowed by `STORAGE_ORIGIN` in the Content-Security-Policy. The logo is an `organization_logo` attachment the worker draws on issued documents.
- Words stay one next-intl file per feature; every `DomainError` reason has its sentence in `errors.json`, kept complete by a test that reads the sources.

**Tech Stack:** plan 5A's, unchanged, with the security release plan 5A's merge brings (next and `@next/eslint-plugin-next` 16.4.1, published 2026-10-14 17:43 UTC; react and react-dom 19.3.1, 2026-10-14 16:47 UTC; `@types/react` and `@types/react-dom` stay 19.3.0, the newest). **No new dependency**: the shadcn components G2 adds (popover, textarea, radio-group, progress, tooltip) come from the registry over plan 5A's `radix-ui` 1.8.1; `packages/api` gains the workspace's `@travel-crm/db` (for `ApiDependencies.db`'s type).

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-foundation-design.md`, sections 6.1 (support's impersonation, its banner and its record), 6.3 (one sign-in page), 7 (the platform console's work: onboarding, plans, subscriptions, the lifecycle, the dashboard), 5 (permanent deletion through the console), 9.2-9.5 (files, PDFs and share links, notifications, the audit log, as screens), 11 (the frontend shell's screens) and 12.1 (gate 6: the journeys, including "an organization in `read_only`" and "impersonation"), with `DESIGN.md` as the design rules. This is plan 5B of the Foundation:

1. Repo and data isolation (done; merged to `main`)
2. API and identity (done; merged to `main`)
3. Shared services (done; merged to `main`)
4. Platform and subscriptions (done; merging after 5A)
5. Web app and release: 5A (the web foundation, done), **5B, this plan** (the remaining screens), 5C (the release)

**Create `apps/web/test/e2e/support/subscriptions.ts`:**

```ts
// Every journey's agency is on a plan with every module, active and paid for a year, as onboarding (plan 4) leaves it:
// without a subscription, request check 2 refuses the agency's every call.
import { planModules } from "@travel-crm/contracts/subscriptions";
import { isUniqueViolation } from "@travel-crm/db";
import type { PlatformClient } from "@travel-crm/db/platform";

/** The key of the plan journeys' agencies are on, the api tests' own. */
export const EVERYTHING_PLAN_KEY = "test-everything";

const everythingPlan = {
  key: EVERYTHING_PLAN_KEY,
  name: "Everything (tests)",
  monthlyPricePaise: 0,
  seatLimit: 1000,
  whatsappNumberLimit: 10,
  storageLimitBytes: 1_000_000_000_000n,
  modules: [...planModules],
};

/** The plan's id. Journeys run at once, so another may create the plan between the look and the create. */
async function everythingPlanId(platform: PlatformClient): Promise<string> {
  const existing = await platform.plan.findUnique({ where: { key: everythingPlan.key }, select: { id: true } });
  if (existing) return existing.id;
  try {
    return (await platform.plan.create({ data: everythingPlan, select: { id: true } })).id;
  } catch (error) {
    if (!isUniqueViolation(error)) throw error;
    return (await platform.plan.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { key: everythingPlan.key }, select: { id: true } })).id;
  }
}

/** Puts the organization on the plan, active and paid for a year from today. */
export async function subscribeToEverything(platform: PlatformClient, organizationId: string): Promise<void> {
  await platform.subscription.create({
    data: {
      organizationId,
      planId: await everythingPlanId(platform),
      billingCycle: "monthly",
      status: "active",
      statusChangedAt: new Date(),
      paidThrough: new Date(Date.now() + 365 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000),
    },
  });
}
```

## Rulings made in planning

Each with why, and the cost if it is wrong. The tracks' own rulings are at the top of each track.

- Ruling: the console is a section of the web app at `/console`, not an app of its own — support's impersonation swaps
  the session cookie on the address that called `/api/auth`, so the agency app must share it; spec 3 puts every call
  on that address; it reuses 5A's components, words and journeys, which 5A ruled stay in `apps/web` — cost if wrong:
  moving `src/console/**` and `src/app/console/**` into an app of its own, the components into `packages/ui`, and a
  session shared across subdomains: a few days.
- Ruling: the console's query cache lives in memory only, nested inside the app's `DataProviders` and built with 5A's
  `createQueryClient` — it then waits for an owed sign-out to settle and refuses and retries as the app does; nothing
  it reads reaches IndexedDB, which a test checks — cost if wrong: console-only cache settings, in one file.
- Ruling: platform staff sign in on the one sign-in page and use the agency's step screens, which follow `?next=` —
  spec 6.3's "one address for everyone"; a step screen opened with `?next=` offers no way around it — cost if wrong: a
  crafted `/change-password?next=/x` hides the way back to the account page.
- Ruling: two-factor is required of platform staff in `staffProcedure` and at Better Auth's impersonation side door,
  and the code step never offers to trust the device on the way to the console — the controller's ruling; the side
  door would otherwise let support impersonate around the console; a trusted device skips the code for 30 days —
  cost if wrong: the api still accepts `trustDevice` from a platform admin who sends it by hand (a before-hook closes
  it; carried forward).
- Ruling: the web app also rewrites `/p/*` and `/webhooks/*` to the api in development, and its service worker leaves
  them to the network — share links are opened on the app's address, and a share link answers with a redirect to
  storage — cost if wrong: none found.
- Ruling: `STORAGE_ORIGIN` joins the CSP's `connect-src` and `img-src`, fixed at build time — `connect-src 'self'`
  refuses the browser's PUT to a presigned URL, and logos load from storage — cost if wrong: a build per storage
  origin (path-style URLs on one regional endpoint share one); a per-request header would lift it.
- Ruling: every `DomainError` reason gets a sentence in `errors.json`, and a test reads the domain's, the api's and
  the api server's sources for them — 5A's carry-forward asked for the typed list of every refusal; the test fails on
  a reason it can't read — cost if wrong: a new way of passing a reason fails the test until it learns it.
- Ruling: `useWriteAccess` decides from `subscription.get` as `assertLifecycleAllows` does, and allows while the
  subscription loads — one source of truth (the test compares every state, kind and role with the domain's own rule);
  the api decides in the end — cost if wrong: a button enabled for a moment, its refusal saying why.
- Ruling: `staff.list` is a `revoke` call — the suspended Owner must see the staff to remove one, and a view is
  refused while suspended — cost if wrong: none (the same people read it as before in every other state).
- Ruling: the logo is an `organization_logo` attachment (PNG or JPEG, at most 1 MB; the newest ready one), not a
  column on the profile, and issued documents freeze its attachment id — no migration, and a document keeps the logo
  it was issued with — cost if wrong: a `logo_attachment_id` column and its migration.
- Ruling: the Foundation's one shareable record is an issued document, and the branding screen's "Preview on a sample
  quotation" issues one (`SMPL-<year>-<n>`, kept like every issued document) — nothing else issues documents before
  quotes (step 3), and it shows the branding on a real PDF — cost if wrong: samples among an agency's documents for
  good (owner question 1).
- Ruling: the browser takes the VAPID public key from `notifications.push.publicKey` — no key in the build, one build
  for every environment — cost if wrong: one request per opt-in.
- Ruling: the journeys start the api, the worker and the console process, and sign platform staff in with two-factor
  on — the console, PDFs, notifications and share links are only real with all three — cost if wrong: about two
  seconds per run.
- Ruling: on phones toasts sit above the bottom bar, and the journeys' axe check waits for transitions with an end —
  a fifth destination put the bar's More button under a toast, and axe measured a toast half faded in — cost if
  wrong: none found.

**Why the tracks never collide.**
- **Shared files are settled first or last.** Groundwork registers every router (empty), adds every message namespace
  (`{}`), every shadcn component and every route, and writes the shared hooks; the tracks fill their own files. The one
  shared line two tracks both touch (`navigation.ts`: S changes the function, A adds an item) is a two-line conflict
  that Task I1 resolves, with the home screen's filter beside it.
- **Journeys make their own data.** Each journey gets a new organization and, in the console, new platform staff;
  every run picks free ports and its own Postgres, MinIO and Mailpit, so seven tracks run their journeys at once.
- **What the tracks need of each other waits for Task I1:** the suspended Owner's staff list, the plan's modules in
  every navigation, two refusal sentences, the unsubscribe link (each asked for in its track's notes).

**Running the tracks.**
- Before a track's first task, make its worktree from Task G2's commit (each track section repeats the command):
  ```bash
  cd /Users/ak/personal/travel-crm && git worktree add ../travel-crm-05b-<track> -b foundation/05b-<track> foundation/05b-screens
  cd /Users/ak/personal/travel-crm-05b-<track> && source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use >/dev/null && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm --filter @travel-crm/db generate && pnpm --filter @travel-crm/brand build && pnpm --filter @travel-crm/web generate
  ```
  with `<track>` one of `subscription`, `business`, `documents`, `notifications`, `audit`, `console-organizations`,
  `console-platform`.
- A track's gate is the whole of `pnpm check`'s parts, the journeys split by project (each section gives the
  commands). Docker is shared with other work: `--concurrency=3`, never restart it, and if it is down, wait and retry.
  Under a load average past 60 the api server's process tests and some journeys time out: rerun once the machine is
  quiet.
- When a track's last task is committed, it is ready to merge (Task I1).

  ```bash
  cd /Users/ak/personal/travel-crm && git worktree add ../travel-crm-05b -b foundation/05b-screens main
  cd /Users/ak/personal/travel-crm-05b && source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use >/dev/null && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm --filter @travel-crm/db generate && pnpm --filter @travel-crm/brand build && pnpm --filter @travel-crm/web generate
  ```
- **Docker must be running**, as for plans 1-5A: the db, domain, integrations and api-server tests and the journeys
  start throwaway containers. Never run `pnpm dev`, `pnpm services:up`, `pnpm db:up` or `docker compose` from a
  worktree while the owner's development services run: the development compose project's name (`travel-crm`) is
  theirs, and compose recreates their containers from the worktree's files.
- **Chromium for the journeys,** once per machine: `pnpm --filter @travel-crm/web exec playwright install chromium`.
- **Pinned versions.** No new package. If a step seems to need one, stop and report.
- **The web app's rules** (ADRs 0018, 0025, 0026) hold, with 5B's: the console imports `type PlatformRouter` only and
  nothing outside `src/console/**` and `src/app/console/**` imports its code (dependency-cruiser); a change's button
  asks `useWriteAccess(kind)`; a new `DomainError` reason needs its sentence in `errors.json`, a new audit action its
  sentence in `audit.json`, a new notification kind its entry in `src/notifications/preferences/kinds.ts` (a test fails
  otherwise); files go straight to storage through `uploadFile`; never show a `.invalid` email; server-rendered HTML
  holds no organization data; colours only from the brand's tokens; every word a message in the feature's file.
- **The product's name** is read from `@travel-crm/brand`, never typed: `packages/brand/test/product-name.test.ts`
  refuses it in any file outside `packages/brand/` and `docs/`. Bidi and control characters in source and tests are
  written as escapes (`\u202E`), never raw.
- **Readable code.** Files stay small and single-purpose; a file over ~200 lines needs a reason. Every source file opens
  with a one-line comment saying what it is for (the shadcn registry's files are the one exception). Comments explain
  *why*. No abbreviations in public names. Strict TypeScript: no `any`, no `!`.
- **Tracks edit only the files the Tracks table gives them.** A track that needs a change elsewhere does the nearest
  thing in its own files and reports it; the change goes into Task I1.
- **Commits.** Conventional Commits, a header of at most 100 characters, staged by name (never `git add -A`, `.` or
  `-a`). The git hooks run Prettier, ESLint and commitlint: fix what they report, never use `--no-verify`. **Never add a
  `Co-Authored-By` trailer.** No secrets or `.env` files in git.
- **Git.** Don't push; there is no remote. Don't touch the main checkout's working tree.

## Review Focus

These failure modes are implied by the spec but easy to miss. Each is pinned by tests in the tasks named.

1. **Every organization's data left where it shouldn't be.** The console reads every agency: its answers must never be
   saved on the device, kept by the service worker, or reach the agency app's cache. Expected: the console's cache is
   memory only and emptied on sign-out; no console page is kept; a member who opens `/console` sees nothing of it.
   Pinned in G1 (`console-gate.test.tsx`: "opens the console for platform staff, on the console's own query cache";
   `test/pwa/shells.test.ts`: "never keeps a console page…"; `console-shell.spec.ts`: an Owner is told the console
   isn't theirs).
2. **Platform staff with less protection than the spec asks.** A new or reset admin reaching the console with only a
   password, support impersonating around the console, a trusted device skipping the code. Expected: a temporary
   password first, then two-factor, before anything; the side door refuses the same; no "trust this device" on the
   way to the console. Pinned in G2 (`platform.test.ts`: "refuses platform staff without two-factor, and lets them in
   once it is on", "asks for the temporary password to be replaced first, then for two-factor"), C2
   (`impersonation-two-factor.test.ts`: "refuses support without two-factor, and starts nothing, until two-factor is
   on"), P3 (`console-staff.spec.ts`: "adds support with a temporary password, which
   they replace, and two-factor on, before the console lets them in") and I1 (`two-factor-challenge.test.tsx`).
3. **An agency allowed more, or less, than its subscription says.** Expected: in read-only every change is disabled
   with the reason and refused by the api, but removing staff, a new password and requiring two-factor stay open; while
   suspended only the Owner keeps them, and can still reach Staff; cancelled, nothing but each person's own account.
   Pinned in G2 (`write-access.test.ts`: every state, kind and role against the domain's rule), S1 (`locks.test.ts`;
   `subscription-locked.spec.ts`; `subscription-read-only.spec.ts`: "an organization in read_only shows the banner on
   every screen"), S2 (`subscription-staff.spec.ts`: "in read-only, an Owner can't add staff, and sees why, but can
   remove someone who left") and I1 (`revoking-access.test.ts`: the suspended Owner lists staff, an Admin can't).
4. **Files that shouldn't be stored or shown.** A type or size the contract refuses, a sensitive file's name or bytes
   reaching a role without `documents:view_sensitive`, an upload that never reached storage shown as done, a logo the
   PDF can't draw. Expected: checked before anything is sent; "Sensitive file" and nothing to do for such a role;
   "didn't reach storage" and nothing confirmed; a logo it can't read left off and the document rendered. Pinned in B2
   (`attachments-panel.test.tsx`: "checks a file's type and size before sending anything", "says when the file didn't
   reach storage, and confirms nothing", "shows a sensitive file only as such…"; `business-files.spec.ts`), G2
   (`upload.test.ts`) and D1 (the PDF and render tests).
5. **A link or redirect that leads off the app, or outlives its use.** A notification's link, a push's tap, a `?next=`
   after a step screen, a share link after it is turned off. Expected: only app paths are followed (else home); a
   revoked link is refused. Pinned in N1 (`notification-bell.test.tsx`: "lists the newest first, and links an item
   only to a path in the app"), N2 (`push-worker.test.ts`: "opens home for anything but a path in the app", "leads home
   from a push without a path in the app"), G1 (`continue-after-step.test.tsx`) and D3
   (`documents-share-links.spec.ts`: "an Owner shares a document by link, sees it opened, and turns the link off").

```
├── packages/api/src/platform/                + two-factor in staffProcedure; organizations.members

│                                               samples; files' systemFile; share links' audit entries
├── packages/integrations/src/pdf/            + the logo on the page
```

Calls only go one way: `apps/web` → `/api` and `/api/platform` over HTTP; in code, `apps/web` → `@travel-crm/brand`,
`@travel-crm/contracts`, `@travel-crm/domain/kernel`, and types from `@travel-crm/api` and `@travel-crm/api/platform`.

## Groundwork

Tasks G1 and G2 run in order on `foundation/05b-screens` in `/Users/ak/personal/travel-crm-05b`.

### Task G1: Platform staff open the console at /console, and the journeys run the whole api

Platform staff now have the console as a section of the web app: `/console` opens on the dashboard (every
organization a page at a time, oldest first, with its status as a dot and a word, days left, seats used of the limit,
last activity and this month's changes and documents), with a sidebar on desktop and a bottom bar on phones that
show Staff to super admins only. A signed-out visitor is sent to sign in and comes back; platform staff who sign in on
the one sign-in page land in the console (the agency's session gate sends them there); a member opening `/console` is
told it is for platform staff; a 401, a temporary password or a missing two-factor sends the person to sign in or to
the step's screen with `?next=`, and the step screens now come back to it. The console has its own query cache, in
memory only, and its own tRPC client at `/api/platform/trpc`, typed by `PlatformRouter` alone; the web app rewrites
that path to `CONSOLE_ORIGIN` before `/api`, and also sends `/p` and `/webhooks` to the api; the service worker keeps
no console page and leaves share links and webhooks to the network. Support stops impersonating from the agency's
banner and is back in the console. The journeys now start the api, the worker and the console process, and sign
platform staff in with two-factor on, so every 5B track can test against all three.

**Create `apps/web/test/account/continue-after-step.test.tsx`:**

```tsx
// After a step the api insisted on, the person goes on to the next step still pending, or to the ?next= page they
// were sent from (the console sends platform staff with one), and home without one: never to another site.
import type { PendingStep } from "@travel-crm/contracts/identity";
import { screen } from "@testing-library/react";
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event";
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import { useContinueAfterStep } from "@/account/current-person";
import { member } from "../support/members";
import { renderScreen } from "./render";

const navigation = vi.hoisted(() => ({ search: "", replace: vi.fn() }));

vi.mock("next/navigation", () => ({
  useRouter: () => ({ push: vi.fn(), replace: navigation.replace }),
  useSearchParams: () => new URLSearchParams(navigation.search),
}));

function Done() {
  const continueAfterStep = useContinueAfterStep();
  return <button onClick={() => void continueAfterStep()}>Done</button>;
}

/** me.get answering as the api does, with the step still pending. */
function meAnswers(pendingStep: PendingStep | null): void {
  vi.stubGlobal(
    "fetch",
    vi.fn(() => Promise.resolve(Response.json([{ result: { data: { ...member(), pendingStep } } }]))),
  );
}

async function finishStep(search: string, pendingStep: PendingStep | null = null): Promise<void> {
  navigation.search = search;
  meAnswers(pendingStep);
  renderScreen(<Done />);
  await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Done" }));
}

afterEach(() => {
  vi.unstubAllGlobals();
  navigation.replace.mockReset();
});

describe("useContinueAfterStep", () => {
  it("goes home when nothing is pending and no ?next= was given", async () => {
    await finishStep("");
    await vi.waitFor(() => {
      expect(navigation.replace).toHaveBeenCalledWith("/");
    });
  });

  it("goes back to the ?next= page when nothing is pending", async () => {
    await finishStep("next=%2Fconsole%2Fplans");
    await vi.waitFor(() => {
      expect(navigation.replace).toHaveBeenCalledWith("/console/plans");
    });
  });

  it("goes on to the step still pending, carrying ?next= along", async () => {
    await finishStep("next=%2Fconsole", "SET_UP_TWO_FACTOR");
    await vi.waitFor(() => {
      expect(navigation.replace).toHaveBeenCalledWith("/two-factor-setup?next=%2Fconsole");
    });
  });

  it("never follows ?next= to another site", async () => {
    await finishStep("next=%2F%2Fevil.example");
    await vi.waitFor(() => {
      expect(navigation.replace).toHaveBeenCalledWith("/");
    });
  });
});
```

```tsx
import { DataProviders, usePageData } from "@/data/providers";
import { locale, messages } from "@/i18n/messages";
import { loadPage, replacePage } from "@/lib/navigate";
import { stubApi } from "../support/api-stub";
import { platformStaff } from "../support/platform-staff";

vi.mock("@/lib/navigate", () => ({ loadPage: vi.fn(), replacePage: vi.fn() }));

const { gate } = messages.console;

/** A console screen, saying whose console it is and which caches hold the console's queries. */
function Screen() {
  const staff = useStaff();
  const consoleQueries = useQueryClient().getQueryCache().getAll().length;
  const appQueries = usePageData().queryClient.getQueryCache().getAll().length;
  return (
    <p>
      Console for {staff.name}, {consoleQueries} console queries, {appQueries} app queries
    </p>
  );
}

function renderGate() {
  return render(
    <NextIntlClientProvider locale={locale} messages={messages}>
      <DataProviders>
        <ConsoleProviders>
          <ConsoleGate>
            <Screen />
          </ConsoleGate>
        </ConsoleProviders>
      </DataProviders>
    </NextIntlClientProvider>,
  );
}

beforeEach(() => {
  window.history.replaceState(null, "", "/console/plans?tier=growth");
});

afterEach(() => {
  vi.unstubAllGlobals();
  vi.mocked(loadPage).mockReset();
  vi.mocked(replacePage).mockReset();
  window.history.replaceState(null, "", "/");
});

describe("ConsoleGate", () => {
  it("opens the console for platform staff, on the console's own query cache", async () => {
    stubApi({ "platform.whoAmI": { data: platformStaff("support") } });
    renderGate();
    expect(await screen.findByText("Console for Arjun Nair, 1 console queries, 0 app queries")).toBeVisible();
  });

  it("tells anyone else the console is for platform staff, and lets them sign out", async () => {
    stubApi({ "platform.whoAmI": { status: 403, reason: "PLATFORM_ONLY" } });
    renderGate();
    expect(await screen.findByText(gate.notStaff)).toBeVisible();
    expect(screen.getByRole("button", { name: messages.console.navigation.signOut })).toBeVisible();
    expect(screen.queryByText(/Console for/)).toBeNull();
  });

  it("sends a signed-out visitor to sign in, and back to this page afterwards", async () => {
    stubApi({ "platform.whoAmI": { status: 401 } });
    renderGate();
    await vi.waitFor(() => {
      expect(loadPage).toHaveBeenCalledWith("/sign-in?next=%2Fconsole%2Fplans%3Ftier%3Dgrowth");
    });
    expect(screen.queryByText(/Console for/)).toBeNull();
  });

  it("sends staff with a temporary password to replace it, and back to this page afterwards", async () => {
    stubApi({ "platform.whoAmI": { status: 403, reason: "CHANGE_PASSWORD" } });
    renderGate();
    await vi.waitFor(() => {
      expect(replacePage).toHaveBeenCalledWith("/change-password?next=%2Fconsole%2Fplans%3Ftier%3Dgrowth");
    });
    expect(screen.queryByText(gate.loadFailed)).toBeNull();
  });

  it("sends staff without two-factor to set it up, and back to this page afterwards", async () => {
    stubApi({ "platform.whoAmI": { status: 403, reason: "SET_UP_TWO_FACTOR" } });
    renderGate();
    await vi.waitFor(() => {
      expect(replacePage).toHaveBeenCalledWith("/two-factor-setup?next=%2Fconsole%2Fplans%3Ftier%3Dgrowth");
    });
  });

  it("says when whoAmI didn't load, and asks again on Try again", async () => {
    const api = stubApi({ "platform.whoAmI": "offline" });
    renderGate();
    // The app's queries try an unanswered call three times, a second and then two apart.
    expect(await screen.findByText(gate.loadFailed, undefined, { timeout: 5_000 })).toBeVisible();
    api.answer("platform.whoAmI", { data: platformStaff("super-admin") });
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: messages.common.tryAgain }));
    expect(await screen.findByText(/Console for Kavita Rao/)).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```

```ts
// The console's navigation: a super admin sees every destination, support all but Staff (platform staff are managed
// by super admins alone, spec 5). Hiding is a convenience; the console's api refuses support's calls there anyway.
// @vitest-environment node
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { consoleRoutes } from "@/console/routes";
import { consoleNavigationItems, isCurrentConsoleItem, visibleConsoleItems } from "@/console/shell/console-navigation";
import { isSuperAdmin } from "@/console/session/staff-context";
import { platformStaff } from "../support/platform-staff";

const keys = (items: { key: string }[]) => items.map((item) => item.key);

describe("visibleConsoleItems", () => {
  it("shows a super admin every destination", () => {
    expect(keys(visibleConsoleItems(platformStaff("super-admin")))).toEqual([
      "home",
      "onboard",
      "plans",
      "jobs",
      "log",
      "staff",
    ]);
  });

  it("shows support everything but Staff", () => {
    expect(keys(visibleConsoleItems(platformStaff("support")))).toEqual(["home", "onboard", "plans", "jobs", "log"]);
  });

  it("leads each item to its console route", () => {
    expect(Object.fromEntries(consoleNavigationItems.map((item) => [item.key, item.href]))).toEqual({
      home: consoleRoutes.home,
      onboard: consoleRoutes.onboard,
      plans: consoleRoutes.plans,
      jobs: consoleRoutes.jobs,
      log: consoleRoutes.log,
      staff: consoleRoutes.staff,
    });
  });
});

describe("isSuperAdmin", () => {
  it("is true for a super admin only", () => {
    expect(isSuperAdmin(platformStaff("super-admin"))).toBe(true);
    expect(isSuperAdmin(platformStaff("support"))).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe("isCurrentConsoleItem", () => {
  const item = (key: string) => {
    const found = consoleNavigationItems.find((candidate) => candidate.key === key);
    if (!found) throw new Error(`no ${key} item`);
    return found;
  };

  it("marks the dashboard only on its own page, and other items on their pages and below", () => {
    expect(isCurrentConsoleItem(item("home"), "/console")).toBe(true);
    expect(isCurrentConsoleItem(item("home"), "/console/plans")).toBe(false);
    expect(isCurrentConsoleItem(item("plans"), "/console/plans")).toBe(true);
    expect(isCurrentConsoleItem(item("plans"), "/console/plans/growth")).toBe(true);
    expect(isCurrentConsoleItem(item("log"), "/console/logbook")).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe("consoleRoutes", () => {
  it("puts an organization's pages under its id", () => {
    const id = "0199a000-0000-7000-8000-000000000002";
    expect(consoleRoutes.organization(id)).toBe(`/console/organizations/${id}`);
    expect(consoleRoutes.dataProtection(id)).toBe(`/console/organizations/${id}/data-protection`);
  });
});
```

```tsx
// The console's frame: its destinations by the person's level (the sidebar on wide screens, the bottom bar and More on
// phones; CSS shows one, so both are here), who is signed in and at which level, and signing out, which empties the
// console's cache and leaves as the app's own sign-out does (data/session.ts).
import "fake-indexeddb/auto";
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { render, screen, within } from "@testing-library/react";
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event";
import { NextIntlClientProvider } from "next-intl";
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import { ConsoleShell } from "@/console/shell/console-shell";
import { StaffProvider } from "@/console/session/staff-context";
import { DataProviders } from "@/data/providers";
import { locale, messages } from "@/i18n/messages";
import { loadPage } from "@/lib/navigate";
import { stubApi } from "../support/api-stub";
import { platformStaff } from "../support/platform-staff";

vi.mock("@/lib/navigate", () => ({ loadPage: vi.fn(), replacePage: vi.fn() }));
vi.mock("next/navigation", () => ({ usePathname: () => "/console" }));

const { navigation } = messages.console;

function renderShell(level: "support" | "super-admin", queryClient = new QueryClient()) {
  return render(
    <NextIntlClientProvider locale={locale} messages={messages}>
      <DataProviders>
        <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
          <StaffProvider staff={platformStaff(level)}>
            <ConsoleShell>
              <p>The page</p>
            </ConsoleShell>
          </StaffProvider>
        </QueryClientProvider>
      </DataProviders>
    </NextIntlClientProvider>,
  );
}

afterEach(() => {
  vi.unstubAllGlobals();
  vi.mocked(loadPage).mockReset();
});

describe("ConsoleShell", () => {
  it("shows a super admin every destination, the page, and who is signed in at which level", async () => {
    stubApi({});
    renderShell("super-admin");
    const sidebar = within(await screen.findByRole("complementary"));
    for (const destination of ["home", "onboard", "plans", "jobs", "log", "staff"] as const) {
      expect(sidebar.getByRole("link", { name: navigation[destination] })).toBeVisible();
    }
    expect(sidebar.getByRole("link", { name: navigation.home })).toHaveAttribute("aria-current", "page");
    expect(screen.getByText("The page")).toBeVisible();
    expect(screen.getByText("Kavita Rao")).toBeVisible();
    expect(screen.getByText(messages.console.levels["super-admin"])).toBeVisible();
  });

  it("shows support no Staff destination", async () => {
    stubApi({});
    renderShell("support");
    const sidebar = within(await screen.findByRole("complementary"));
    expect(sidebar.queryByRole("link", { name: navigation.staff })).toBeNull();
    expect(screen.getByText(messages.console.levels.support)).toBeVisible();
  });

  it("keeps the rest in More on a phone, Staff among them for a super admin", async () => {
    stubApi({});
    renderShell("super-admin");
    await userEvent.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: navigation.more }));
    const sheet = await screen.findByRole("dialog");
    expect(within(sheet).getByRole("link", { name: navigation.log })).toBeVisible();
    expect(within(sheet).getByRole("link", { name: navigation.staff })).toBeVisible();
    expect(within(sheet).getByRole("button", { name: navigation.signOut })).toBeVisible();
  });

  it("signs out: the console's cache empties, the api is told, and the sign-in page loads", async () => {
    const api = stubApi({ "auth/sign-out": { data: {} } });
    const queryClient = new QueryClient();
    queryClient.setQueryData(["platform", "dashboard"], { organizations: ["Sharma Travels"] });
    renderShell("support", queryClient);
    const sidebar = await screen.findByRole("complementary");
    await userEvent.click(within(sidebar).getByRole("button", { name: navigation.signOut }));
    await vi.waitFor(() => {
      expect(loadPage).toHaveBeenCalledWith("/sign-in");
    });
    expect(queryClient.getQueryCache().getAll()).toEqual([]);
    await vi.waitFor(() => {
      expect(api.calls).toContain("auth/sign-out");
    });
  });
});
```

```tsx
// The console's dashboard (spec 7.4): every organization a page at a time, oldest first, with its status as a dot and
// a word, days left, seats used of the limit, last activity and this month's usage, each leading to the
// organization's page; and honest loading, empty and error states.
import type { OrganizationOverview } from "@travel-crm/contracts/platform";
import { render, screen, within } from "@testing-library/react";
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event";
import { NextIntlClientProvider } from "next-intl";
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import { ConsoleProviders } from "@/console/data/console-providers";
import { DashboardScreen } from "@/console/dashboard/dashboard-screen";
import { PLATFORM_TIME_ZONE } from "@/console/platform-time-zone";
import { locale, messages } from "@/i18n/messages";
import { formatDay } from "@/lib/format";
import { stubApi } from "../support/api-stub";
import { screenIs } from "../organization/render";

const { dashboard, status } = messages.console;

const lastActiveAt = "2026-10-14T06:30:00.000Z";

function overview(overrides: Partial<OrganizationOverview> = {}): OrganizationOverview {
  return {
    organizationId: "0199a000-0000-7000-8000-000000000002",
    name: "Sharma Travels",
    code: "SHARMA",
    status: "active",
    planName: "Growth",
    nextChangeOn: "2026-10-27",
    daysLeft: 12,
    seats: { used: 3, limit: 10 },
    storage: { usedBytes: 0, limitBytes: null },
    lastActiveAt,
    thisMonth: { changes: 1234, documentsIssued: 5 },
    ...overrides,
  };
}

function renderDashboard() {
  return render(
    <NextIntlClientProvider locale={locale} messages={messages}>
      <ConsoleProviders>
        <DashboardScreen />
      </ConsoleProviders>
    </NextIntlClientProvider>,
  );
}

afterEach(() => {
  vi.unstubAllGlobals();
});

describe("DashboardScreen", () => {
  it("shows each organization's row in a table on wide screens, leading to its page", async () => {
    screenIs("wide");
    stubApi({ "platform.dashboard.organizations": { data: { organizations: [overview()], nextCursor: null } } });
    renderDashboard();
    const link = await screen.findByRole("link", { name: /Sharma Travels/ });
    expect(link).toHaveAttribute("href", "/console/organizations/0199a000-0000-7000-8000-000000000002");
    const row = within(link.closest("tr") ?? document.body);
    expect(row.getByText("SHARMA")).toBeVisible();
    expect(row.getByText(status.active)).toBeVisible();
    expect(row.getByText("12 days")).toBeVisible();
    expect(row.getByText("3 of 10")).toBeVisible();
    expect(row.getByText(formatDay(new Date(lastActiveAt), { timeZone: PLATFORM_TIME_ZONE }))).toBeVisible();
    expect(row.getByText("1,234")).toBeVisible();
    expect(row.getByText("5")).toBeVisible();
    expect(screen.queryByRole("button", { name: dashboard.showMore })).toBeNull();
  });

  it("says what isn't there: no subscription, no limit, no change due, never active", async () => {
    screenIs("wide");
    const bare = overview({
      status: null,
      planName: null,
      daysLeft: null,
      nextChangeOn: null,
      seats: { used: 1, limit: null },
      lastActiveAt: null,
    });
    stubApi({ "platform.dashboard.organizations": { data: { organizations: [bare], nextCursor: null } } });
    renderDashboard();
    const row = within((await screen.findByRole("link", { name: /Sharma Travels/ })).closest("tr") ?? document.body);
    expect(row.getByText(status.none)).toBeVisible();
    expect(row.getByText(dashboard.noChangeDue)).toBeVisible();
    expect(row.getByText("1, no limit")).toBeVisible();
    expect(row.getByText(dashboard.neverActive)).toBeVisible();
  });

  it("lists organizations on a phone, name and status first", async () => {
    screenIs("phone");
    stubApi({ "platform.dashboard.organizations": { data: { organizations: [overview()], nextCursor: null } } });
    renderDashboard();
    const link = await screen.findByRole("link", { name: /Sharma Travels/ });
    expect(link).toHaveAttribute("href", "/console/organizations/0199a000-0000-7000-8000-000000000002");
    expect(within(link).getByText(status.active)).toBeVisible();
    expect(within(link).getByText("3 of 10")).toBeVisible();
    expect(screen.queryByRole("table")).toBeNull();
  });

  it("shows the next page below the first when asked", async () => {
    screenIs("wide");
    const first = overview({ organizationId: "0199a000-0000-7000-8000-000000000011", name: "Sharma Travels" });
    const second = overview({ organizationId: "0199a000-0000-7000-8000-000000000012", name: "Iyer Holidays" });
    const api = stubApi({
      "platform.dashboard.organizations": { data: { organizations: [first], nextCursor: first.organizationId } },
    });
    renderDashboard();
    await screen.findByRole("link", { name: /Sharma Travels/ });
    api.answer("platform.dashboard.organizations", { data: { organizations: [second], nextCursor: null } });
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: dashboard.showMore }));
    expect(await screen.findByRole("link", { name: /Iyer Holidays/ })).toBeVisible();
    expect(screen.getByRole("link", { name: /Sharma Travels/ })).toBeVisible();
    expect(screen.queryByRole("button", { name: dashboard.showMore })).toBeNull();
  });

  it("asks for the next page after the last organization of the page before", async () => {
    screenIs("wide");
    const first = overview({ organizationId: "0199a000-0000-7000-8000-000000000011" });
    const api = stubApi({
      "platform.dashboard.organizations": { data: { organizations: [first], nextCursor: first.organizationId } },
    });
    renderDashboard();
    await screen.findByRole("link", { name: /Sharma Travels/ });
    api.answer("platform.dashboard.organizations", { data: { organizations: [], nextCursor: null } });
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: dashboard.showMore }));
    await vi.waitFor(() => {
      expect(inputsSent()).toEqual([{ limit: 25 }, { limit: 25, after: first.organizationId }]);
    });
  });

  it("says when there are no organizations yet, and leads to onboarding the first", async () => {
    screenIs("wide");
    stubApi({ "platform.dashboard.organizations": { data: { organizations: [], nextCursor: null } } });
    renderDashboard();
    expect(await screen.findByText(dashboard.empty)).toBeVisible();
    expect(screen.getByRole("link", { name: dashboard.onboardFirst })).toHaveAttribute(
      "href",
      "/console/organizations/new",
    );
  });

  it("says when the organizations didn't load, and loads them on Try again", async () => {
    screenIs("wide");
    const api = stubApi({ "platform.dashboard.organizations": { status: 403 } });
    renderDashboard();
    expect(await screen.findByText(dashboard.loadFailed)).toBeVisible();
    api.answer("platform.dashboard.organizations", { data: { organizations: [overview()], nextCursor: null } });
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: messages.common.tryAgain }));
    expect(await screen.findByRole("link", { name: /Sharma Travels/ })).toBeVisible();
  });
});

/** The inputs the dashboard's calls sent, read from the stubbed fetch's URLs. */
function inputsSent(): unknown[] {
  const fetch = vi.mocked(globalThis.fetch);
  return fetch.mock.calls.map(([input]) => {
    const url = new URL(input instanceof Request ? input.url : String(input), "http://localhost");
    const batch = JSON.parse(url.searchParams.get("input") ?? "{}") as Record<string, unknown>;
    return batch["0"];
  });
}
```

```ts
});
```

**Create `apps/web/test/e2e/console-shell.spec.ts`:**

```ts
// The console at /console (ADR 0019): a signed-out visitor signs in and comes back to it, platform staff who sign in
// on the one sign-in page land on its dashboard, support sees no Staff destination, an agency's Owner is told it
// isn't theirs, and support stops impersonating from the agency's banner, back in the console. Each journey's last
// screen also gets the automatic accessibility check (support/accessible-after-each.ts).
import type { Page, TestInfo } from "@playwright/test";
import { expect, signInToConsole, test, type PlatformStaff } from "./support/console";
import { signInByEmail } from "./support/fixtures";
import { totpCode } from "./support/totp";

const isPhone = (testInfo: TestInfo) => testInfo.project.name === "phone";

/** Signs in on the sign-in screen: the email and password, then the code from the authenticator app. */
async function signInOnScreen(page: Page, staff: PlatformStaff): Promise<void> {
  await page.getByRole("textbox", { name: "Email" }).fill(staff.email);
  await page.getByLabel("Password").fill(staff.password);
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Sign in" }).click();
  await page.getByLabel("Code from your authenticator app").fill(totpCode(staff.totpSecret));
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Continue" }).click();
}

const dashboardHeading = (page: Page) => page.getByRole("heading", { level: 1, name: "Dashboard" });

test("a signed-out visitor to the console signs in and comes back to it", async ({ page, support }) => {
  await page.goto("/console");
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/sign-in\?next=%2Fconsole$/);
  await signInOnScreen(page, support);
  await expect(dashboardHeading(page)).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/console$/);
  await expect(page).toHaveTitle(/^Dashboard · Console · /);
});

test("platform staff who sign in on the sign-in page land on the dashboard, every organization on it", async ({
  page,
  superAdmin,
  agency,
}) => {
  await page.goto("/sign-in");
  await signInOnScreen(page, superAdmin);
  await expect(dashboardHeading(page)).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/console$/);
  // Oldest first, a page at a time: this journey's agency is among the newest. Its code tells it from the others.
  const organization = page.getByRole("link").filter({ hasText: agency.code });
  const showMore = page.getByRole("button", { name: "Show more organizations" });
  while (!(await organization.isVisible())) {
    await expect(showMore.or(organization)).toBeVisible();
    if (await showMore.isVisible()) await showMore.click();
  }
  await expect(organization).toHaveAttribute("href", `/console/organizations/${agency.organizationId}`);
  await expect(organization).toContainText(agency.name);
});

async function destinations(page: Page, testInfo: TestInfo): Promise<string[]> {
  if (!isPhone(testInfo)) {
    return page
      .getByRole("navigation", { name: "Console" })
      .filter({ visible: true })
      .getByRole("link")
      .allTextContents();
  }
  const bar = await page
    .getByRole("navigation", { name: "Console" })
    .filter({ visible: true })
    .getByRole("link")
    .allTextContents();
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "More" }).click();
  const more = await page.getByRole("dialog").getByRole("link").allTextContents();
  return [...bar, ...more];
}

test("support sees every destination but Staff, a super admin sees Staff too", async ({
  page,
  support,
  superAdmin,
}, testInfo) => {
  await signInToConsole(page, superAdmin);
  await page.goto("/console");
  await expect(dashboardHeading(page)).toBeVisible();
  expect(await destinations(page, testInfo)).toEqual(["Dashboard", "Onboard", "Plans", "Jobs", "Log", "Staff"]);

  await page.context().clearCookies();
  await page.goto("/console");
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/sign-in\?next=%2Fconsole$/);
  await signInToConsole(page, support);
  await page.goto("/console");
  await expect(dashboardHeading(page)).toBeVisible();
  expect(await destinations(page, testInfo)).toEqual(["Dashboard", "Onboard", "Plans", "Jobs", "Log"]);
  // At the foot of the sidebar, or atop the phone's More sheet, which destinations() left open.
  await expect(page.getByText("Arjun Nair").filter({ visible: true })).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByText("Support", { exact: true }).filter({ visible: true })).toBeVisible();
});

test("an agency's Owner opening the console is told it isn't theirs", async ({ page, agency }) => {
  await signInByEmail(page, agency.owner);
  await page.goto("/console");
```

**Create `apps/web/test/e2e/support/console.ts`:**

```ts
// Platform staff for the console's journeys, made in the database as the api's tests make them (a platform role, a
// password account, no membership), with two-factor turned on through Better Auth's own endpoints, as staff do on the
// setup screen. signInToConsole signs them in through /api/auth as the sign-in screen does: the password, then the
// authenticator's code.
import { request as playwrightRequest, type Page } from "@playwright/test";
import type { PlatformClient } from "@travel-crm/db/platform";
import type { Identity } from "@travel-crm/domain/identity";
import { expect, test as base } from "./fixtures";
import { secretOf, totpCode } from "./totp";

export interface PlatformStaff {
  userId: string;
  name: string;
  email: string;
  password: string;
  level: "support" | "super-admin";
  /** The authenticator secret: two-factor is on (the console requires it from Task G2). */
  totpSecret: string;
}

/** Better Auth's user.role for each level (packages/domain/src/identity/access.ts). */
const roleOf = { support: "admin", "super-admin": "super-admin" } as const;

function originHeader(): { origin: string } {
  return { origin: process.env.E2E_BASE_URL ?? "" };
}

async function createPlatformStaff(
  database: { identity: Identity; platform: PlatformClient },
  baseURL: string,
  level: PlatformStaff["level"],
  name: string,
): Promise<PlatformStaff> {
  const email = `${level}-${crypto.randomUUID()}@platform.test`;
  const password = "platform-password-1";
  const hash = await (await database.identity.auth.$context).password.hash(password);
  const user = await database.platform.user.create({
    data: { name, email, role: roleOf[level], mustChangePassword: false },
  });
  await database.platform.account.create({
    data: { userId: user.id, accountId: user.id, providerId: "credential", password: hash },
  });
  // Turned on in a browser context of its own, so the journey's page starts signed out.
  const api = await playwrightRequest.newContext({ baseURL });
  try {
    const headers = originHeader();
    expect((await api.post("/api/auth/sign-in/email", { data: { email, password }, headers })).ok()).toBe(true);
    const enabled = await api.post("/api/auth/two-factor/enable", { data: { password }, headers });
    expect(enabled.ok()).toBe(true);
    const totpSecret = secretOf(((await enabled.json()) as { totpURI: string }).totpURI);
    const verified = await api.post("/api/auth/two-factor/verify-totp", {
      data: { code: totpCode(totpSecret) },
      headers,
    });
    expect(verified.ok()).toBe(true);
    return { userId: user.id, name, email, password, level, totpSecret };
  } finally {
    await api.dispose();
  }
}

export const test = base.extend<{ superAdmin: PlatformStaff; support: PlatformStaff }>({
  superAdmin: async ({ database, baseURL }, use) => {
    await use(await createPlatformStaff(database, baseURL ?? "", "super-admin", "Kavita Rao"));
  },
  support: async ({ database, baseURL }, use) => {
    await use(await createPlatformStaff(database, baseURL ?? "", "support", "Arjun Nair"));
  },
});

export { expect };

/**
 * Signs platform staff in through the api, as the sign-in screen does: the password, which asks for a code, then the
 * authenticator's code. Better Auth 1.7.7 takes a code again within its 30 seconds, as the setup's was.
 */
export async function signInToConsole(page: Page, staff: PlatformStaff): Promise<void> {
  const headers = originHeader();
  const signedIn = await page.request.post("/api/auth/sign-in/email", {
    data: { email: staff.email, password: staff.password },
    headers,
  });
  expect(signedIn.ok()).toBe(true);
  expect(await signedIn.json()).toMatchObject({ twoFactorRedirect: true });
  const verified = await page.request.post("/api/auth/two-factor/verify-totp", {
    data: { code: totpCode(staff.totpSecret) },
    headers,
  });
  expect(verified.ok()).toBe(true);
}
```

Replace:

```ts

/** Waits until url answers 200, for up to a minute, failing at once if the process serving it stops. */
async function waitUntilUp(url: string, server: Started): Promise<void> {
  const answering = async () => {
    for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 120; attempt += 1) {
      try {
        if ((await fetch(url)).ok) return;
      } catch {
        // Not listening yet.
      }
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 500));
    }
    throw new Error(`${url} didn't come up within a minute`);
  };
  await Promise.race([answering(), server.exited]);
}
```

with:

```ts

/** Waits until ready() holds, checking every half second for up to a minute, failing at once if the process stops. */
async function waitUntil(what: string, ready: () => Promise<boolean>, server: Started): Promise<void> {
  const waiting = async () => {
    for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 120; attempt += 1) {
      if (await ready()) return;
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 500));
    }
    throw new Error(`${what} didn't come up within a minute`);
  };
  await Promise.race([waiting(), server.exited]);
}

/** Waits until url answers 200. */
function waitUntilUp(url: string, server: Started): Promise<void> {
  return waitUntil(
    url,
    () =>
      fetch(url).then(
        (response) => response.ok,
        () => false,
      ),
    server,
  );
}
```

```ts
    const vapid = vapidKeys();
    /** What the api's three commands all read (apps/api/src/environment.ts). */
    const apiEnvironment: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = {
      ...process.env,
      NODE_ENV: "development",
      PORT: String(apiPort),
      DATABASE_URL: databaseUrl,
      BETTER_AUTH_SECRET: "e2e-only-secret-".padEnd(48, "x"),
      // Browsers reach the api through the web app's address (spec 3), so that is its URL and the trusted origin.
      BETTER_AUTH_URL: webUrl,
      APP_URL: webUrl,
      TRUSTED_ORIGINS: "",
      // Journeys sign in many times from one address.

      // Plan 3's services are configured from the environment, all of them real: the api refuses to start without

      ...storage,
      ...email,
      EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS: "no-reply@travel-crm.localhost",
      VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY: vapid.publicKey,
      VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY: vapid.privateKey,
      VAPID_SUBJECT: "mailto:dev@travel-crm.localhost",
    };
    const tsx = path.join(apiDirectory, "node_modules/.bin/tsx");
    await reserved.release();
    const api = start(tsx, ["src/server.ts"], { cwd: apiDirectory, env: apiEnvironment });
    const worker = start(tsx, ["src/worker.ts"], { cwd: apiDirectory, env: apiEnvironment });
    const platformConsole = start(tsx, ["src/console.ts"], {
      cwd: apiDirectory,
      // As apps/api/src/console-environment.ts reads them.
      env: { ...apiEnvironment, DATABASE_PLATFORM_URL: platformDatabaseUrl, CONSOLE_PORT: String(consolePort) },
    });
    const web = start(process.execPath, ["server.js"], {
      cwd: standalone,
      env: { ...process.env, NODE_ENV: "production", PORT: String(webPort), HOSTNAME: "127.0.0.1" },
    });
    started.push(api, worker, platformConsole, web);
    await waitUntilUp(`${apiUrl}/health`, api);
    await waitUntilUp(`${consoleUrl}/health`, platformConsole);
    // The worker has no port; it says when its jobs and listeners are running.
    await waitUntil("the worker", () => Promise.resolve(worker.output().includes("worker running")), worker);
    await waitUntilUp(webUrl, web);
```

**Create `apps/web/test/shell/stop-impersonating.test.tsx`:**

```tsx
// Support stops impersonating from the banner (spec 6.1): Better Auth gives the session back to support, the device
// forgets the member's data, and the console opens. A stop the api refused says why, and nothing is wiped.
import "fake-indexeddb/auto";
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { render, screen } from "@testing-library/react";
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event";
import { NextIntlClientProvider } from "next-intl";
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import { Toaster } from "@/components/ui/sonner";
import type { AuthClient } from "@/data/auth-client";
import { locale, messages } from "@/i18n/messages";
import { loadPage } from "@/lib/navigate";
import { StopImpersonatingButton } from "@/shell/stop-impersonating";

vi.mock("@/lib/navigate", () => ({ loadPage: vi.fn(), replacePage: vi.fn() }));

const { banners } = messages.shell;

function renderButton(stopImpersonating: AuthClient["stopImpersonating"]) {
  const queryClient = new QueryClient();
  queryClient.setQueryData(["staff", "list"], [{ name: "Ravi Kumar" }]);
  render(
    <NextIntlClientProvider locale={locale} messages={messages}>
      <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
        <StopImpersonatingButton auth={{ stopImpersonating }} />
        <Toaster />
      </QueryClientProvider>
    </NextIntlClientProvider>,
  );
  return queryClient;
}

afterEach(() => {
  vi.mocked(loadPage).mockReset();
});

describe("StopImpersonatingButton", () => {
  it("stops, forgets the member's data, then opens the console", async () => {
    const stop = vi.fn(() => Promise.resolve({ ok: true as const, data: null }));
    const queryClient = renderButton(stop);
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: banners.stop }));
    await vi.waitFor(() => {
      expect(loadPage).toHaveBeenCalledWith("/console");
    });
    expect(stop).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
    expect(queryClient.getQueryCache().getAll()).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("says why a stop failed, and keeps the page as it is", async () => {
    const stop = vi.fn(() =>
      Promise.resolve({ ok: false as const, status: 0, code: "NETWORK", retryAfterSeconds: null }),
    );
    const queryClient = renderButton(stop);
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: banners.stop }));
    expect(await screen.findByText(messages.errors.network)).toBeVisible();
    expect(loadPage).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(queryClient.getQueryCache().getAll()).toHaveLength(1);
  });
});
```

```ts
/**
 * Where /api/* goes (spec 3): the browser always calls the api on the address it loaded the app from, so cookies stay
 * first-party and the api needs no CORS. Rewrites are fixed when the app is built, so this is for development and the
 * end-to-end tests. A deployment routes /api/* to the api at its load balancer, before Next.js sees the request, so a
 * production build without API_ORIGIN has no rewrite at all: an /api request that reaches the app is a 404, never one
 * quietly sent to whatever listens on localhost.
 */

```

with:

```ts
/**
 * Where a rewrite goes (spec 3): the browser always calls the api and the console on the address it loaded the app
 * from, so cookies stay first-party and neither needs CORS. Rewrites are fixed when the app is built, so this is for
 * development and the end-to-end tests. A deployment routes these paths at its load balancer, before Next.js sees the
 * request, so a production build without the setting has no rewrite to it at all: a request that reaches the app is a
 * 404, never one quietly sent to whatever listens on localhost.
 */
function originSetting(name: "API_ORIGIN" | "CONSOLE_ORIGIN", developmentDefault: string): string | null {
  const value = process.env[name];
  if (value) return checkedOrigin(name, value, developmentDefault);
  return production ? null : developmentDefault;
}

/** The api: its tRPC and sign-in at /api, and the share links (/p) and webhooks it serves on the app's address. */
const apiOrigin = originSetting("API_ORIGIN", "http://localhost:3001");
/** The console process (ADR 0019): the console's tRPC at /api/platform/trpc. */
const consoleOrigin = originSetting("CONSOLE_ORIGIN", "http://localhost:3002");

/** The console's rewrite comes first: /api/platform/... matches /api/:path* too, which would send it to the api. */
function rewrites() {
  const toConsole =
    consoleOrigin === null
      ? []
      : [{ source: "/api/platform/:path*", destination: `${consoleOrigin}/api/platform/:path*` }];
  const toApi =
    apiOrigin === null
      ? []
      : ["/api", "/p", "/webhooks"].map((prefix) => ({
          source: `${prefix}/:path*`,
          destination: `${apiOrigin}${prefix}/:path*`,
        }));
  return [...toConsole, ...toApi];
}

```

```tsx
"use client";

// /two-factor-setup: the setup, then on to whatever the api still asks, or back to the ?next= page, or home.
import { CurrentPersonGate, useContinueAfterStep, useReturnPath } from "./current-person";
```

```tsx
// Every console screen (spec 7, ADR 0019): the console's own data layer, the gate that lets platform staff in, then
// the console's frame around the page. Its pages are titled "<screen> · Console · <product>".
import { brand } from "@travel-crm/brand";
import type { Metadata } from "next";
import { getTranslations } from "next-intl/server";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { ConsoleProviders } from "@/console/data/console-providers";
import { ConsoleGate } from "@/console/session/console-gate";
import { ConsoleShell } from "@/console/shell/console-shell";

export async function generateMetadata(): Promise<Metadata> {
  const t = await getTranslations("console");
  const consoleTitle = `${t("title")} · ${brand.productName}`;
  return { title: { default: consoleTitle, template: `%s · ${consoleTitle}` } };
}

export default function ConsoleLayout({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <ConsoleProviders>
      <ConsoleGate>
        <ConsoleShell>{children}</ConsoleShell>
      </ConsoleGate>
    </ConsoleProviders>
  );
}
```

**Create `apps/web/src/console/dashboard/dashboard-screen.tsx`:**

```tsx
"use client";

// The console's dashboard (spec 7.4): every organization with its status, days left, seats used of the limit, last
// activity and this month's usage, oldest first, a page at a time. Loading shows rows of skeleton; an empty platform
// leads to onboarding the first organization; a failure says so with a Retry.
import { BuildingIcon } from "lucide-react";
import Link from "next/link";
import { useTranslations } from "next-intl";
import { Delayed } from "@/components/delayed";
import { EmptyState } from "@/components/empty-state";
import { ErrorState } from "@/components/error-state";
import { PageTitle } from "@/components/page-title";
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";
import { Skeleton } from "@/components/ui/skeleton";
import { Spinner } from "@/components/ui/spinner";
import { useWideScreen } from "@/lib/use-wide-screen";
import { consoleRoutes } from "../routes";
import { OrganizationsList } from "./organizations-list";
import { OrganizationsTable } from "./organizations-table";
import { useOrganizationsOverview } from "./use-organizations-overview";

export function DashboardScreen() {
  const t = useTranslations("console.dashboard");
  const tCommon = useTranslations("common");
  const wide = useWideScreen();
  const overview = useOrganizationsOverview();
  const { organizations } = overview;

  let content;
  if (organizations === undefined) {
    content = overview.isError ? (
      <ErrorState message={t("loadFailed")} retryLabel={tCommon("tryAgain")} onRetry={() => void overview.refetch()} />
    ) : (
      <Delayed>
        <div role="status" aria-busy="true" aria-label={t("loading")} className="flex flex-col gap-2">
          {[0, 1, 2].map((row) => (
            <Skeleton key={row} className="h-14 w-full" />
          ))}
        </div>
      </Delayed>
    );
  } else if (organizations.length === 0) {
    content = (
      <EmptyState
        icon={BuildingIcon}
        message={t("empty")}
        action={
          <Button asChild>
            <Link href={consoleRoutes.onboard}>{t("onboardFirst")}</Link>
          </Button>
        }
      />
    );
  } else {
    content = (
      <>
        {wide ? (
          <OrganizationsTable organizations={organizations} />
        ) : (
          <OrganizationsList organizations={organizations} />
        )}
        {overview.hasNextPage && (
          <Button
            variant="outline"
            className="self-center"
            disabled={overview.isFetchingNextPage}
            onClick={() => void overview.fetchNextPage()}
          >
            {overview.isFetchingNextPage && <Spinner />}
            {overview.isFetchingNextPage ? t("loadingMore") : t("showMore")}
          </Button>
        )}
      </>
    );
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-6">
      <PageTitle>{t("title")}</PageTitle>
      {content}
    </div>
  );
}
```

**Create `apps/web/src/console/dashboard/organizations-list.tsx`:**

```tsx
"use client";

// The dashboard's organizations on phones (DESIGN.md section 6): a divided list, each organization leading to its
// page, with its name and status on the first line and its figures below. Names wrap rather than being cut off.
import type { OrganizationOverview } from "@travel-crm/contracts/platform";
import Link from "next/link";
import { useTranslations } from "next-intl";
import { consoleRoutes } from "../routes";
import { SubscriptionStatusBadge } from "../subscription-status";
import { useOverviewFigures, type OverviewFigures } from "./overview-figures";

const FIGURES: readonly (keyof OverviewFigures)[] = ["daysLeft", "seats", "lastActive", "changes", "documents"];

export function OrganizationsList({ organizations }: { organizations: OrganizationOverview[] }) {
  const t = useTranslations("console.dashboard");
  const figuresOf = useOverviewFigures();
  return (
    <ul className="divide-y rounded-lg border">
      {organizations.map((organization) => {
        const figures = figuresOf(organization);
        return (
          <li key={organization.organizationId}>
            <Link
              href={consoleRoutes.organization(organization.organizationId)}
              className="flex flex-col gap-1 px-4 py-3 hover:bg-accent"
            >
              <span className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
                <span className="font-medium text-primary break-words script-leading">{organization.name}</span>
                <SubscriptionStatusBadge status={organization.status} />
              </span>
              <span className="text-caption text-muted-foreground">
                <span className="numbers">{organization.code}</span>
                {organization.planName !== null && ` · ${organization.planName}`}
              </span>
              <span className="flex flex-wrap gap-x-4 gap-y-1 text-label">
                {FIGURES.map((figure) => (
                  <span key={figure}>
                    <span className="text-muted-foreground">{t(`columns.${figure}`)}</span>{" "}
                    <span className="numbers">{figures[figure]}</span>
                  </span>
                ))}
              </span>
            </Link>
          </li>
        );
      })}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

```tsx
"use client";

// The dashboard's organizations on tablets and wider (DESIGN.md section 6): a table, numbers mono and right-aligned,
// each organization's name leading to its page. Names wrap rather than being cut off.
import type { OrganizationOverview } from "@travel-crm/contracts/platform";
import Link from "next/link";
import { useTranslations } from "next-intl";
import { Table, TableBody, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow } from "@/components/ui/table";
import { consoleRoutes } from "../routes";
import { SubscriptionStatusBadge } from "../subscription-status";
import { useOverviewFigures } from "./overview-figures";

export function OrganizationsTable({ organizations }: { organizations: OrganizationOverview[] }) {
  const t = useTranslations("console.dashboard");
  const figuresOf = useOverviewFigures();
  return (
    <Table>
      <TableHeader>
        <TableRow>
          <TableHead scope="col">{t("columns.organization")}</TableHead>
          <TableHead scope="col">{t("columns.status")}</TableHead>
          <TableHead scope="col" className="text-right">
            {t("columns.daysLeft")}
          </TableHead>
          <TableHead scope="col" className="text-right">
            {t("columns.seats")}
          </TableHead>
          <TableHead scope="col" className="text-right">
            {t("columns.lastActive")}
          </TableHead>
          <TableHead scope="col" className="text-right">
            {t("columns.changes")}
          </TableHead>
          <TableHead scope="col" className="text-right">
            {t("columns.documents")}
          </TableHead>
        </TableRow>
      </TableHeader>
      <TableBody>
        {organizations.map((organization) => {
          const figures = figuresOf(organization);
          return (
            <TableRow key={organization.organizationId}>
              <TableCell className="whitespace-normal">
                <Link
                  href={consoleRoutes.organization(organization.organizationId)}
                  className="flex flex-col py-1 hover:underline"
                >
                  <span className="font-medium text-primary script-leading">{organization.name}</span>
                  <span className="text-caption text-muted-foreground">

                    {organization.planName !== null && ` · ${organization.planName}`}
                  </span>
                </Link>
              </TableCell>
              <TableCell>
                <SubscriptionStatusBadge status={organization.status} />
              </TableCell>
              <TableCell className="numbers text-right">{figures.daysLeft}</TableCell>
              <TableCell className="numbers text-right">{figures.seats}</TableCell>
              <TableCell className="numbers text-right">{figures.lastActive}</TableCell>
              <TableCell className="numbers text-right">{figures.changes}</TableCell>
              <TableCell className="numbers text-right">{figures.documents}</TableCell>
            </TableRow>
          );
        })}
      </TableBody>
    </Table>
  );
}
```

```ts
"use client";

// One organization's figures on the dashboard, as words: days left, seats used of the limit, last activity and this
// month's counts, in Indian formats, the dates as India's clocks show them.
import type { OrganizationOverview } from "@travel-crm/contracts/platform";
import { useTranslations } from "next-intl";
import { useCallback } from "react";
import { formatCount, formatDay } from "@/lib/format";
import { PLATFORM_TIME_ZONE } from "../platform-time-zone";

export interface OverviewFigures {
  daysLeft: string;
  seats: string;
  lastActive: string;
  changes: string;
  documents: string;
}

export function useOverviewFigures(): (organization: OrganizationOverview) => OverviewFigures {
  const t = useTranslations("console.dashboard");
  return useCallback(
    ({ daysLeft, seats, lastActiveAt, thisMonth }: OrganizationOverview) => ({
      daysLeft: daysLeft === null ? t("noChangeDue") : t("daysLeft", { count: daysLeft }),
      seats:
        seats.limit === null
          ? t("seatsNoLimit", { used: formatCount(seats.used) })
          : t("seats", { used: formatCount(seats.used), limit: formatCount(seats.limit) }),
      lastActive:
        lastActiveAt === null ? t("neverActive") : formatDay(new Date(lastActiveAt), { timeZone: PLATFORM_TIME_ZONE }),
      changes: formatCount(thisMonth.changes),
      documents: formatCount(thisMonth.documentsIssued),
    }),
    [t],
  );
}
```

**Create `apps/web/src/console/dashboard/use-organizations-overview.ts`:**

```ts
"use client";

// The dashboard's organizations a page at a time (dashboard.organizations), oldest first: each page asks for those
// after the last organization of the page before.
import { useInfiniteQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { useConsoleTRPC, useConsoleTRPCClient } from "../data/console-trpc";

export const ORGANIZATIONS_PER_PAGE = 25;

export function useOrganizationsOverview() {
  const trpc = useConsoleTRPC();
  const client = useConsoleTRPCClient();
  const query = useInfiniteQuery({
    queryKey: [...trpc.dashboard.organizations.pathKey(), { limit: ORGANIZATIONS_PER_PAGE }],
    queryFn: ({ pageParam }) =>
      client.dashboard.organizations.query({
        limit: ORGANIZATIONS_PER_PAGE,
        ...(pageParam === null ? {} : { after: pageParam }),
      }),
    initialPageParam: null as string | null,
    getNextPageParam: (page) => page.nextCursor,
  });
  return { ...query, organizations: query.data?.pages.flatMap((page) => page.organizations) };
}
```

**Create `apps/web/src/console/data/console-providers.tsx`:**

```tsx
"use client";

// The console's data layer, inside the app's (data/providers.tsx, which settles an owed sign-out before anything
// asks who is signed in): a query cache of its own, in memory only and never saved to IndexedDB, since the console
// sees every organization, and the console's tRPC client. A refused call takes platform staff where the console's
// api says, coming back to this page afterwards: a 401 to sign in, a pending step to its screen.
import { QueryClientProvider } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { useState, type ReactNode } from "react";
import { createQueryClient } from "@/data/query-client";
import { loadPage, replacePage } from "@/lib/navigate";
import { pendingStepRoute, signInRoute } from "@/lib/routes";
import { ConsoleTRPCProvider, createConsoleClient } from "./console-trpc";

const currentPage = () => `${window.location.pathname}${window.location.search}`;

export function ConsoleProviders({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const [consoleClient] = useState(createConsoleClient);
  const [queryClient] = useState(() => {
    const client = createQueryClient({
      // A full page load, which also drops this cache from memory.
      onSignedOut: () => {
        client.clear();
        loadPage(signInRoute(currentPage()));
      },
      // In place of this page, as the app does, so Back doesn't return to a screen that couldn't load.
      onPendingStep: (step) => {
        replacePage(pendingStepRoute(step, currentPage()));
      },
    });
    return client;
  });
  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <ConsoleTRPCProvider trpcClient={consoleClient} queryClient={queryClient}>
        {children}
      </ConsoleTRPCProvider>
    </QueryClientProvider>
  );
}
```

```ts
// The console's tRPC client and its TanStack Query hooks (ADR 0019). The web app knows the console's procedures only
// by the PlatformRouter type; calls go to /api/platform/trpc on the address the app was loaded from, which reaches
// the console process (a rewrite in development, the load balancer when deployed), batched like the api's.
import type { PlatformRouter } from "@travel-crm/api/platform";
import { createTRPCClient, httpBatchLink } from "@trpc/client";
import { createTRPCContext } from "@trpc/tanstack-react-query";

export const {
  TRPCProvider: ConsoleTRPCProvider,
  useTRPC: useConsoleTRPC,
  useTRPCClient: useConsoleTRPCClient,
} = createTRPCContext<PlatformRouter>();

export function createConsoleClient() {
  return createTRPCClient<PlatformRouter>({ links: [httpBatchLink({ url: "/api/platform/trpc" })] });
}

export type ConsoleClient = ReturnType<typeof createConsoleClient>;
```

**Create `apps/web/src/console/session/console-gate.tsx`:**

```tsx
"use client";

// The way into the console. whoAmI says who is signed in; until it answers the screen shows a skeleton. Anyone who
// isn't platform staff (an agency's member, support while impersonating) is told the console isn't theirs. A 401 or
// a pending step is the data layer's to act on (console-providers.tsx), so nothing shows meanwhile; any other failure
// says so with a Retry.
import { useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { useTranslations } from "next-intl";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { Delayed } from "@/components/delayed";
import { ErrorState } from "@/components/error-state";
import { Skeleton } from "@/components/ui/skeleton";
import { refusalOf } from "@/data/api-error";
import { useConsoleTRPC } from "../data/console-trpc";
import { ConsoleSignOutButton } from "../shell/console-sign-out";
import { StaffProvider } from "./staff-context";

/** Refusals the data layer answers by loading another page. */
const LEAVING = new Set(["CHANGE_PASSWORD", "SET_UP_TWO_FACTOR"]);

export function ConsoleGate({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  const t = useTranslations("console.gate");
  const tCommon = useTranslations("common");
  const trpc = useConsoleTRPC();
  const whoAmI = useQuery(trpc.whoAmI.queryOptions());

  if (whoAmI.data) return <StaffProvider staff={whoAmI.data}>{children}</StaffProvider>;
  if (whoAmI.isError) {
    const refusal = refusalOf(whoAmI.error);
    if (refusal?.status === 401 || LEAVING.has(refusal?.reason ?? "")) return null;
    if (refusal?.reason === "PLATFORM_ONLY") {
      return (
        <div className="mx-auto flex max-w-[40ch] flex-col items-center gap-4 px-4 py-16 text-center">
          <p>{t("notStaff")}</p>
          <ConsoleSignOutButton />
        </div>
      );
    }
    return (
      <ErrorState message={t("loadFailed")} retryLabel={tCommon("tryAgain")} onRetry={() => void whoAmI.refetch()} />
    );
  }
  return (
    <Delayed>
      <div role="status" aria-busy="true" aria-label={t("loading")} className="flex min-h-dvh">
        <Skeleton className="hidden w-58 md:block" />
        <div className="flex flex-1 flex-col gap-4 p-6">
          <Skeleton className="h-9 w-64" />
          <Skeleton className="h-40 w-full max-w-[1200px]" />
        </div>
      </div>
    </Delayed>
  );
}
```

**Create `apps/web/src/console/session/staff-context.tsx`:**

```tsx
"use client";

// Who is signed in to the console (whoAmI): their name and level, for every console screen. The console gate
// provides it once whoAmI has answered, so screens never see a missing person.
import type { PlatformWhoAmIOutput } from "@travel-crm/contracts/platform";
import { createContext, useContext, type ReactNode } from "react";

/** Platform staff as the console shows them: support, or a super admin, who also manages plans and staff. */
export type ConsoleStaff = PlatformWhoAmIOutput;

const StaffContext = createContext<ConsoleStaff | null>(null);

export function StaffProvider({ staff, children }: { staff: ConsoleStaff; children: ReactNode }) {
  return <StaffContext value={staff}>{children}</StaffContext>;
}

export function useStaff(): ConsoleStaff {
  const staff = useContext(StaffContext);
  if (!staff) throw new Error("useStaff() is for screens inside the console's gate");
  return staff;
}

/** For showing or hiding things only: the console's api refuses support what is a super admin's (spec 5). */
export function isSuperAdmin(staff: Pick<ConsoleStaff, "level">): boolean {
  return staff.level === "super-admin";
}
```
